s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic, pruritic rash with firm, red-brown plaques on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk in a patient with a history of systemic sclerosis
salient_findings: Firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale on the proximal upper extremities and anterior trunk
Nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles on lesional punch biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 60s
Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis
Patient has tried treating the rash with topical aloe without improvement
Review of systems is negative for new or worsening constitutional, respiratory, or gastrointestinal symptoms
Patient has a history of heart failure, interstitial lung disease, sclerodactyly, and Raynaud phenomenon
Patient is receiving mycophenolate mofetil, 1 g twice daily
Complete blood cell count with differential is unremarkable
Tissue cultures are negative for bacteria, fungus, and acid-fast bacillus
Lesional punch biopsy specimens show nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles

shortlist.label: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis and is receiving mycophenolate mofetil, which may be related to nephrogenic systemic fibrosis

shortlist.label: Scleromyxedema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a pruritic rash with firm, red-brown plaques, which is consistent with scleromyxedema

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Lesional punch biopsy specimens show nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers, which is consistent with eosinophilic fasciitis

shortlist.label: Morphea
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic sclerosis and presents with a localized, pruritic rash, which may be related to morphea

shortlist.label: Lichen sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with a pruritic rash and has a history of systemic sclerosis, which may be related to lichen sclerosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of firm, red-brown plaques without overlying scale, combined with the histopathological findings of nodular proliferations of thick collagen fibers in large fascicles, is consistent with eosinophilic fasciitis. The patient's history of systemic sclerosis and the absence of skin tightening in the affected areas also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis
rejected.why: The patient's kidney function is not mentioned as being impaired, and the presentation does not include the typical features of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis, such as thickening and hardening of the skin.

rejected.label: Scleromyxedema
rejected.why: The patient's presentation lacks the characteristic mucin deposition and lichenoid papules seen in scleromyxedema.

rejected.label: Morphea
rejected.why: The patient's lesions do not exhibit the typical features of morphea, such as well-demarcated, sclerotic plaques with overlying skin tightening.

rejected.label: Lichen sclerosis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not include the characteristic features of lichen sclerosis, such as thin, white, wrinkled skin with purpura and scarring.
